reference: https://www.neea.edu.cn/res/Home/1704/55b02330ac17274664f06d9d3db8249d.pdf — CET 2016 syllabus reading requirements, used only as a general reading reference. Existing product combines CET4/CET6/TOEFL; this is NOT an official equivalence or an individual test-score calibration.
audience: The existing combined college English / CET4_6_TOEFL product band. Use general college-level reading, supported abstract ideas and introductory academic contexts. Do not silently interpret this mixed band as advanced TOEFL or CET6-only proficiency; technical terms needed for the clue must be explained or inferable.
grammarReference: Complex clauses, passive voice, nonfinite constructions, contrast and supported multi-step inference are acceptable if relations are clear in the text. Distinguish language comprehension from specialist disciplinary knowledge. Academic topics are permitted; unexplained jargon and knowledge outside the text must not be necessary.

examples.context: Because the results could not be repeated, the researchers questioned whether their conclusion was reliable.
examples.assessment: General academic reasoning is supported explicitly; complex wording alone is not grounds for rejection.

examples.context: The conclusion rests on heteroskedasticity-consistent asymptotics.
examples.assessment: Specialist statistical concepts are required without explanation; replace the support language.

rules: Evaluate vocabulary IN ITS ACTUAL SENSE and collocation, syntax, inference/background knowledge, and ALL distractors. Assuming the learner knows the target sense, can they understand the clues and distinguish the choices?

Use the local vocabulary hints as evidence, not a whitelist. Listed words can have unfamiliar senses. Unlisted names, transparent derivations, explained terms and incidental details can be acceptable. Do not impose a one-new-word rule or a count/percentage threshold.

Do not reject by sentence length, number of clauses, punctuation or historical/religious/scientific topic. Prefer natural meaningful context. Identify an actual comprehension barrier, not merely a long or rare-looking word.

Core clues should remain accessible without knowing another harder unglossed word. A cluster of unfamiliar terms can obstruct understanding even when no single term is indispensable. Do not exempt distractors just because the target is advanced.

Use suitable only when all four dimensions are supported. Borderline means a concrete unresolved comprehension concern; unsuitable means an identified blocking requirement. Replace only the problematic context or distractors; preserve the target meaning. Do not make the item ambiguous to simplify it.
